hardware_label: Measured on 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13420H (laptop-4c); not a Raspberry Pi, not embedded hardware
profile_claim: Scaling with core count on the development laptop. One-way inference only: a miss here makes a miss on a Raspberry Pi 5 very likely; a pass says nothing about the Pi.

verdicts.question: Did the pipeline meet the 100 ms deadline?
verdicts.statement: No. 100.0 % of 798 frames missed 100 ms. Median latency 676 ms is 6.8x the deadline; P99 is 1816 ms.
verdicts.rule: pass: 0 violations; warn: 0 < violations <= 5 %; fail: violations > 5 %. Violation = per-frame pipeline latency (preprocess + register) strictly greater than the deadline.

verdicts.question: Did registration produce valid matches?
verdicts.statement: 269 of 269 registrations passed the validity gate (100.0 %).
verdicts.rule: pass: >= 99 % accepted; warn: >= 90 %; fail: < 90 %. Accepted = passes the registration validity gate.

verdicts.question: How accurate was the estimated trajectory?
verdicts.statement: ATE RMSE 0.51 m (max 1.06 m) over 22.5 m of ground-truth path after rigid alignment; position RPE is reported per window in the summary. Both include any unmodelled sensor-to-body offset (lever arm) between the estimate and the ground-truth body frame, so they mix drift with extrinsic bias. Scan-to-scan odometry has no loop closure, so error accumulates with distance.
verdicts.rule: descriptive; no pass/fail threshold is applied to accuracy
